pt-idempotency.title: One charge, any number of retries
pt-idempotency.description: The client sends the same key on every retry, the server inserts a key row under a unique constraint, calls the provider with the key, and stores the response to replay to later retries.
pt-idempotency.note: Keep the key with the effect it guards, not in a separate cache.

pt-outbox.title: An order and its event commit together
pt-outbox.description: The order and an outbox row commit in one transaction, a relay publishes the row and marks it sent, and consumers deduplicate by event ID in case it is published twice.
pt-outbox.note: A crash can repeat an event on this path but cannot lose a committed one.

pt-retries.title: How a 30-second slowdown becomes a lasting outage
pt-retries.description: A brief slowdown causes timeouts, retries raise load from 800 to 3,200 requests per second, the queue stays full of work for callers who left, and a retry budget caps load at 880 so the queue drains.
pt-retries.note: Backoff spreads retries, jitter decorrelates them, a budget caps their total.

pt-protect.title: Four ways to keep slow work from spreading
pt-protect.description: A timeout stops waiting for one call, a circuit breaker stops calling for a while, a fallback returns a partial page, and load shedding has the server refuse work to save the rest.
pt-protect.note: Timeouts and breakers act in the caller; shedding acts in the busy server.

items.title: Load shedding
items.detail: refuse work to save the rest

pt-backpressure.title: Four answers when the queue is full
pt-backpressure.description: At its limit a queue can block the producer, reject new work with a clear error, drop the oldest items when fresh data replaces stale data, or spill to disk, which is a larger and still finite queue.
pt-backpressure.note: An unbounded queue only defers this choice until memory runs out.

pt-stampede.title: What each defense does when keys expire
pt-stampede.description: With no protection 1,000 readers hit the database, single-flight lets one caller rebuild a key, jittered expiry spreads when keys expire, and serving stale returns the old value while one worker refreshes it.
pt-stampede.note: Jitter spreads many keys. It does not help one hot key.
